codeReview.summary: This feature produced a consolidated benchmark report at .flywheel/benchmark-report.md by compiling data from two source reports (tests/e2e/benchmark-full-mode.md and tests/e2e/benchmark-sprint-mode.md). The implementation is a pure documentation artifact — no code changes, only a 132-line markdown file. All data points were cross-referenced against the source reports and are accurate. The report satisfies all four required sections: (1) 6-row table with Prompt/Mode/Runtime/Quality/Notes, (2) latency pattern summary with aggregate statistics and per-prompt speedup, (3) quality assessment methodology with 4-dimension scoring rubric, (4) review-triggers-fix flow observations. The commit was force-added because .flywheel/ is gitignored by the parent monorepo .gitignore. VAL-BENCH-001 (latency table) and VAL-BENCH-002 (quality scores) are both fulfilled.

issues.description: The file is in .flywheel/ which is gitignored by the parent monorepo .gitignore. It was force-added with 'git add -f', which works but is fragile — future contributors running 'git add .' won't pick it up, and 'git clean -fd' would delete it. The source reports live in tests/e2e/ which is tracked normally. Consider placing the consolidated report alongside them (e.g., tests/e2e/benchmark-consolidated.md) or adding an explicit negation in .gitignore (e.g., '!flywheel-tui/.flywheel/benchmark-report.md').

All 6 runs received identical quality scores of 4/5 with the same justification ('focused narrowly on the prompt'). While this may be accurate for these simple prompts, uniform scores reduce the discriminatory value of the quality dimension. A brief note acknowledging this limitation (e.g., 'N=6 with identical complexity class limits score variance') would strengthen the methodology section.
